_comment: Reusable team template for Luma AMD Speedrun optimization sessions. Strip session-specific fields before use. Reconstitute with: TeamCreate(team_name='speedrun-sN') + Agent(subagent_type=..., name=..., prompt=...).
_usage: 1. TeamCreate({team_name: 'speedrun-sN', description: '...'}) 2. TaskCreate for each task below 3. Agent for each member below (knowledge-curator in background, kernel-researcher foreground)

team_structure.description: Luma AMD Speedrun optimization — Direct CK dispatch breakthrough team

members.name: knowledge-curator
members.role: Populates SurrealDB + Obsidian vault with all session findings. Runs in background — independent of other agents.

members.name: kernel-researcher
members.description: Discover MLA kernel argument layout from aiter source
members.role: Clones aiter repo, traces C++ dispatch layer, extracts kernel argument struct. Critical path — dispatch engineer depends on this.

members.name: dispatch-engineer
members.role: Implements hipModuleLaunchKernel-based submission.py. Spawned AFTER kernel-researcher returns arg layout. Runs popcorn-cli test then benchmark.

task_template.subject: Populate SurrealDB knowledge graph with all session findings
Create Obsidian vault notes with wikilinks for luma-speedrun knowledge base
Discover MLA stage1 kernel argument layout from aiter C++ source
Implement MLA direct CK dispatch submission (hipModuleLaunchKernel)
Fuse MLA stage1 + reduce with direct dispatch (if C.1 correct)
MoE direct dispatch via fmoe_2stages kernels (if MLA validates approach)

knowledge_curator.summary: Store all N experiments, M blockers, and their bidirectional edges in SurrealDB + create Obsidian vault notes at ~/vaults/cohezion-vault/luma-speedrun/. Each experiment node: {kernel, approach, session, status, score_us, finding, evidence}. Each blocker node: {description, resolved, resolution}. Create README.md as entry point with [[wikilinks]] graph. Create per-experiment notes in experiments/, per-blocker notes in blockers/, discovery notes in discoveries/, approach notes in approaches/.
knowledge_curator.template_note: Update experiment list + blocker list each session before spawning. The vault README format and wikilink structure stays constant.

kernel_researcher.summary: Check ~/dev/aiter exists. If not: git clone https://github.com/ROCm/aiter ~/dev/aiter --depth=1. Search csrc/ for hipModuleLaunchKernel + target kernel name. Read C++ binding to extract: (1) GRID dims, (2) BLOCK dims, (3) SHARED_MEM size, (4) exact argument order + types. Also find reduce kernel .co filename. Write spec to luma_speedrun/amd-mixed-mla/probes/kernel_arg_spec.md and ~/vaults/cohezion-vault/luma-speedrun/discoveries/D004-mla-stage1-arg-layout.md. Return full spec in response.
kernel_researcher.template_note: Per-session: update target kernel name + Python call signature. The research methodology (clone → grep csrc → read binding) stays constant.

dispatch_engineer.summary: Given kernel arg spec from kernel-researcher: implement submission_direct_ck.py. Pre-load hip module + function handle at module import time (outside custom_kernel). In hot path: build ctypes void** arg array matching spec exactly. Use torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream for HIP stream. Run popcorn-cli --mode test FIRST, then --mode benchmark only if test passes. Submit --mode leaderboard only if >5% improvement over baseline.
dispatch_engineer.template_note: Per-session: update arg array construction from spec. The overall pattern (pre-load → build args → launch) stays constant.

vault_structure.README.md: Entry point with status table + dead ends + wikilink graph
vault_structure.experiments/: One note per experiment: {status, finding, evidence, links}
vault_structure.blockers/: Active and resolved blockers with resolution path
vault_structure.discoveries/: Confirmed findings that enable future approaches

known_dead_ends.reason: K!=V dims (576 vs 512) forces 1542µs slow path on gfx950
CK cache is shape-keyed, no collision between 8-expert warmup and 256-expert production
Runner sandbox blocks aiter source reads via glob/inspect
Same timing as aiter (~22us), quantization is the real bottleneck
Runner profiling-level stream monitor blocks any kernel launched on non-harness hipStream_t. torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream is NOT the harness stream.
torch.cuda.graph() creates internal side stream during capture — same 'work on another stream' violation. CUDA graph capture is blocked even though individual aiter calls are fine.

_stream_detection_note: Session 3 discovery (D005): The harness stream handle is NEVER exposed to user code. Any GPU dispatch that bypasses PyTorch's standard kernel dispatch machinery (ctypes, CUDA graphs, manual HIP streams) will fail. Only torch.* and aiter.* calls correctly target the harness timing stream via PyTorch's C++ dispatch layer.

runner_environment.submission_constraint: Single submission.py file only — no multi-file, no HIP compilation
